title: Lean redesign of a silver diamine fluoride pathway in 23 school dental clinics: timely treatment and acceptability reported side by side
abstract: Problem: only 41 percent of children with an active cavity received silver diamine fluoride at the next school clinic visit. Intervention: lean redesign with a combined consent form and staining photograph, a need-ordered call list, a staining leaflet and bilingual calls. Measures: the proportion treated within 42 days of screening by home language (measurement strand) and the acceptability of the pathway to parents, teachers and therapists (conversation strand), reported side by side. Results will follow the project.
introduction: Silver diamine fluoride arrests most cavities, but school programmes lose time waiting for consent, and staining on front teeth is unacceptable to many parents. Families with limited majority-language proficiency return fewer consent forms.
methods: Value stream mapping, three test cycles, programme records analysed as p-charts by home language, and structured conversations analysed with framework analysis; ethics approval PHU-REC-2026-22.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present the two strands in separate sections and a side-by-side table.
discussion: The discussion will ask whether the two strands agree, what informed refusals mean for the measure, and whether any language group was left behind.
limitations: Uncontrolled time series; six-school conversation sample; baseline for the 42-day window recomputed from records.
conclusion: To be written after the project, strand by strand.
reportingChecklist: SQUIRE 2.0, with COREQ items for the conversation strand
summary: Draft with two strands kept separate and results left empty.
